match_question_text: Three resistors each having value 'R' are connected as shown in figure. What is the equivalence resistance between 'X' and 'Y'?

set.explanation_short: The three resistors are joined end to end in one path from X to Y, so they are in series: R + R + R = 3R.
set.explanation_long: Follow the wire from X: it passes through the first R, then a connecting wire leads to the second R, then to the third R and on to Y. There is only one path for the current, so the resistors are in series and their resistances add: R_eq = R + R + R = 3R. R/3 would be three in parallel; R³ is not dimensionally a resistance.
set.explanation_trick: One path for current = series = add the resistances.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — that is a single resistor.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — R/3 is for three equal resistors in parallel.
explanation_options.c: Correct — three R in series give 3R.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — resistances add; they are never multiplied.

match_question_text: The diagram shows a wire, carrying a current 'I', placed between the poles of magnet: In which direction does the force on the wire act?
match_option_a: Towards the 'N' pole of the magnet

set.explanation_short: F = IL × B: current up the page and field from N to S give a force into the page — 'downwards' when the diagram is viewed from above.
set.explanation_long: The field between the poles runs from N to S (left to right) and the current flows up the page. By Fleming's left-hand rule (or F = IL × B), the force is perpendicular to both, pointing into the page. The figure is a top view of the magnet, so into the page is downwards. The force is never along the field, so it is not towards either pole.
set.explanation_trick: Force ⊥ both I and B; a force pointing into the page of a top view is 'downwards'.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — the force is perpendicular to the field, not along it towards N.
explanation_options.b: Correct — the force points into the page, i.e. downwards.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — this is the reverse of the force direction.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — the force is perpendicular to the field, not towards S.

match_question_text: The nature of an aqueous solution of ammonia (NH3) is:

set.explanation_short: Aqueous ammonia is basic: NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻.
set.explanation_long: Ammonia dissolves in water and takes a proton from it: NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻. The hydroxide ions make the solution basic (a weak base, pH about 11 for a dilute solution); it turns red litmus blue and neutralises acids to give ammonium salts. It does not react with bases, so it is not amphoteric. (The printed UHS key marks A, amphoteric, but the solution is basic, so D is used.)
set.explanation_trick: NH₃ in water → NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ → basic.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — an amphoteric substance (e.g. Al(OH)₃, ZnO) reacts with both acids and bases; aqueous ammonia only behaves as a base.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — the OH⁻ formed raises the pH above 7.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — ammonia accepts a proton; it does not release H⁺ in water.
explanation_options.d: Correct — aqueous ammonia is a weak base.

match_question_text: The reaction of two amino acid molecules (glycine + glycine) shown in the figure gives a product called a dipeptide molecule. Which structure correctly represents that dipeptide?

set.question_text: The reaction H₂N–CH₂–COOH + H₂N–CH₂–COOH → ? gives a product called dipeptide molecule represented by:
set.explanation_short: Two glycine molecules join by a peptide bond, –CO–NH–, giving H₂N–CH₂–CO–NH–CH₂–COOH (glycylglycine).
set.explanation_long: A peptide bond forms when the –COOH of one amino acid condenses with the –NH₂ of the other and a molecule of water is lost. The carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to the nitrogen: H₂N–CH₂–CO–NH–CH₂–COOH. Options A, B and C all put an oxygen between carbon and nitrogen (a C–O–N link), which is not a peptide bond. (The printed UHS key marks A, but A has a C–O–N link, so D is used.)
set.explanation_trick: Peptide bond = C(=O) bonded straight to N–H; no oxygen between C and N.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — the –CO–O–NH– link has an extra oxygen between the carbonyl carbon and nitrogen.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — no C=O on the first unit, a C–O–N link and a charged nitrogen.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — the first unit has lost its C=O and is joined through oxygen.
explanation_options.d: Correct — –CO–NH– joins the two glycine units.

match_question_text: The formula of 'Zwitter ion' is represented by (R = side chain):

set.question_text: The formula of 'Zwitter ion' is represented by:
set.explanation_short: A zwitterion carries –NH₃⁺ and –COO⁻ (= –CO₂⁻) on the same molecule: H₃N⁺–CH(R)–CO₂⁻.
set.explanation_long: In an amino acid the basic –NH₂ group takes the proton released by the acidic –COOH group, so the molecule carries both a positive and a negative charge: H₃N⁺–CH(R)–CO₂⁻. The carboxylate keeps both oxygens. Option A prints the carboxylate as CO⁻ with one oxygen missing, which is not a real group. (The printed UHS key marks A, but C is the complete, correct formula, so C is used.)
set.explanation_trick: Zwitterion = NH₃⁺ + COO⁻, both on the α-carbon.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — 'CO⁻' has lost an oxygen; the carboxylate is CO₂⁻.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — nitrogen bonded to carbon cannot also carry four hydrogens.
explanation_options.c: Correct — protonated amino group and complete carboxylate.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — NH₂⁺ bonded to one carbon has too few hydrogens for a positive nitrogen.

match_question_text: Final acceptor of electrons in respiratory chain is:
A biochemical process which occurs within a cell to breakdown complex compounds to produce energy is called:

set.explanation_short: Respiration is the process in a cell that breaks down complex food compounds to release energy.
set.explanation_long: Cellular respiration is the name of the biochemical process in which glucose and other complex compounds are broken down inside the cell and the energy released is stored as ATP. It proceeds through oxidation-reduction reactions, but 'oxidation reduction' is a type of chemical reaction, not the name of this cellular process. Photosynthesis builds compounds, and photophosphorylation is ATP synthesis driven by light. (The printed UHS key marks C, but the process defined here is respiration, so A is used.)
set.explanation_trick: Breakdown for energy = respiration; build-up using light = photosynthesis.

explanation_options.a: Correct — respiration breaks down complex compounds to release energy.
explanation_options.b: Wrong — photosynthesis makes complex compounds and stores energy.
explanation_options.c: Wrong — redox reactions occur in respiration, but that is a reaction type, not the name of the process.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — photophosphorylation is ATP formation in the light reactions of photosynthesis.

match_question_text: Cystic fibrosis patient lack a gene that codes for trans-membrane carrier of??
In an ecosystem mycorrhizae are an example of:

set.explanation_short: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association of a fungus with plant roots; the UHS key marks symbiosis.
set.explanation_long: A mycorrhiza is a close, long-term association between a fungus and the roots of a plant: the fungus takes up water and minerals for the plant, and the plant supplies sugars to the fungus. In the textbook it is given as an example of symbiosis. Because both partners benefit, the association is also correctly described as mutualism, which is one kind of symbiosis, so option C is also scientifically sound. The UHS key marks B.
set.explanation_trick: Symbiosis is the umbrella term; mutualism (both benefit), commensalism and parasitism are its kinds.

explanation_options.a: Wrong — in predation one organism kills and eats the other.
explanation_options.b: Correct (UHS key) — mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association.
explanation_options.c: Also accurate — it is a mutualistic kind of symbiosis, but the key marks B.
explanation_options.d: Wrong — in parasitism one partner is harmed.
